sentences.text: Vide the present appeal, the order dated 01.05.2019 has been challenged vide which Ld.Adjudicating Officer/ADM(New Delhi) ("AO" in short) dismissed the application filed by Food Safety Officer (FSO in short) against all the respondents.
The appeal was presented before this court on 26.07.2019.
2. The present appeal has been filed on 26.07.2019 alongwith an application for condonation of delay.
In the application for condonation of delay, it has been submitted that the impugned order passed on 01.05.2019 was received by the department on 16.05.2019.

Thereafter, Sh. Hukam Singh,
FSO of this case was on special duty from 21.05.2019 to 25.05.2019.

sentences.text: 1 FSO was on earned leave.

It has further been submitted that on 03.06.2019, 06.06.2019 &
11.06.2019, FSO attended various courts for hearing in departmental cases.
Thereafter, the FSO was on earned leave from 19.06.2019 to 30.06.2019.

It has been submitted that after going through the impugned order and material on record, FSO prepared detailed note with reasons to file appeal in the present case and forwarded the same to Sh. A. K. Singh, DO(HQ) to seek legal opinion as well as approval of Commissioner, Food Safety.
DO (HQ) then forwarded the file to DO Prosecution/Deputy Legal Advisor on 02.07.2019 for his opinion.
It has been submitted that DLA Prosecution gave detailed opinion on 09.07.2019 opining the matter fit for appeal and forwarded the file to Commissioner, Food Safety for approval.
On 17.07.2019, Commissioner, Food Safety accorded his approval to file an appeal and on 18.07.2019, file was forwarded to Chief Public Prosecutor to file an appeal.
Chief Public Prosecutor took some time to file the appeal.
Thus, the appeal could not be filed within limitation period.
Ld. Chief PP submitted that the delay is caused due to official reason and not a deliberate one.
3. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for respondents has submitted that this appeal is liable to be dismissed.
It has been submitted that the limitation period is of 30 days and this court can maximum condone the delay for another 30 days.
However, this appeal is filed after delay of ten days.
4. I have heard the submissions and perused the record.
5. Section 3.3.1 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 ("FSS Rules" in short) provides as under: "3.3.1 Appeal to Appellate tribunal 1. Limitation for filing appeal:

Every appeal under section 70 of the Act, arising out of a decision of the Adjudicating Officer appointed under section 68 of the Act, shall be filed within a period of 30 days from the date on which the copy of the order against which the appeal is filed, is received by the appellant.

Provided, however, that the Appellate Tribunal may allow a maximum of another 30 days to entertain an appeal if it is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing the appeal within first 30 days."

A bare perusal of above FSS Rules, makes it clear that after the expiry of 30 days which is a limitation of filing of the appeal u/S 70 FSS Act, the Appellate Tribunal has a discretion to allow a maximum of another 30 days to entertain the appeal.
This extension can only be granted if the Appellate Tribunal is satisfied that there are sufficient cause for not filing the appeal.
6. In the present case, the impugned order was passed on 01.05.2019.
The plea of the department was that the copy of the impugned order was received on 16.05.2019.
However, the present appeal was filed in the court on 26.07.2019.
Therefore, there is a delay of around one month and ten days.
Rule 3.3.1(1) FSS Rules provides limitation of 30 days for filing of the appeal from the date on which the copy of the order against which the appeal is filed, is received by the appellant.
However, the law confers that the Appellate Tribunal may allow maximum of another 30 days, if it is satisfied that there are sufficient cause for not filing the appeal within first 30 days.

Thus as per law, the Tribunal Food Safety Officer vs )Sh. Tarkeshwar Prasad Singh on 16 September, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127565481/
2 has maximum discretion to condone the delay of another 30 days, if the expiry of first 30 days is described under the law.

sentences.text: Even for condoning the delay of 30 days there has to be sufficient cause for non filing of the appeal.
The plea of the department is that after the copy of the impugned order was received, the concerned official was either attending to the courts or was on earned leave.
The reason explained is not at all sufficient reason.
If the concerned official was on leave, the duty of the Supervisory Officer was to ensure that the work is not stopped.
The limitation cannot be extended on such a filmsy ground that either the official was busy in official work or was on earned leave.
Every public official has a duty to attend to his official work which also includes ensuring that the law is followed strictly.
If the delay in filing the appeal are condoned on such ground every second official will come to court and seek enlargement of time on the ground that either he was busy or was on earned leave.
This at all cannot be permitted.
I consider that there are no sufficient grounds for condoning the delay in filing the appeal.
Hence, the appeal being barred by limitation is dismissed.
